I originally got this game for my children.  And then I shoved them aside and played through the game myself, cause I was hooked.  I grew up loving both Legos and Marvel.  This is a fantastic merger of both.  

Pros:
- This game has a lighthearted storyline that doesn't take itself too seriously.  
- The antics and quips made by the characters are humorous and satiristically appropriate.  
- Kid appropriate means that I can sit down with my children for an hour or two to 'bond.'
- Marvel.

Neutral:
- Gameplay is typical of most lego games; get coins, find gold/red bricks, unlock characters.

Cons:
- It does get a bit repetative sometimes; gameplay and 'flavor' dialogue.
- There are a few bugs still in the game.  Though they don't crop up all that often, it is annoying to have to quit a level simply because the bug prevented your advance.
- Flight controls were terrible (or I'm old, and just don't get it).

This is by far the greatest Lego game I have played since The Complete Saga. Not only does the game feature a huge roster of playable characters who actually have the personality and abilities of those they represent, but the game also features a unique storyline where the voice acting actually fits the game. 

The story is fantastic this time around. The voice acting being recorded specifically for the game helps it to not be as cheesy or low quality as before. The cinematics then also can be how they used to be and have a lot more fun and freedom without havign to fit within a prerecorded audio clip.

The characters are as high quality as they are numerous. Multiple characters and costumes leave almost no one out (except nightcrawler...) and will have a few choices for everyone. They each are unique and are fun to play and although I do wish Hulk could scale buildings they stick pretty close to th source. 

Manhattan is a great hub area featuring TONS of content to do either while between missions or at the end of the game and are just looking for tokens for new characters and vehicles.

Combat has also been improved where each character has their signature moves and bad guys actually can be comboed and used to make tons of studs. Speaking of studs, there is no lack of them here and you will be hitting 1 millions before half way through the game.

Overall it was the best in the series and I really could not think of much to improve on other then some wonky flight controls and some races that were a bit unfair in that regard. BUY THIS!

LEGO® Marvel™ Super Heroes is a true LOVE LETTER to the Marvel Universe. It features characters from Iron man to Wolverine. From Spider-man to The Silver Surfer. It even has Stan Lee singing the Merry Marvel Marching Society song at the end... what a true love letter indeed to the MCU. Even in 2023 onward, this game stands out amongst all the other recent MARVEL games and LEGO games to date. With a few technical issues here and there, which stops it being a true masterpiece, it easy, is one of the BEST LEGO games and SUPERHERO games you can play or buy on the marketplace.

[h1][b] Pros [/b][/h1] 
⚫Well, from the very start the story made sense. It was about the heroes trying to collect the cosmic bricks around the world before the villains do. It was a very coherent story compared to the disastrous Lego Marvel's Avengers.
⚫So you can go from playing a mission with the Hulk and Iron man to a mission with the Fantastic Four and then to a mission with the X-Men and not be confused on what is happening at all. 
⚫Now, If you have played Lego's Marvel Avengers you will know that the AUDIO is a joke. Well, never fear as the audio in LEGO® Marvel™ Super Heroes is done to PERFECTION. 
⚫The puzzles in this game are really enjoyable. Not over the top repetitive either. They done a REALLY good job with making the puzzles in this game.
⚫Compared to Lego Marvel's Avengers.... this game has a MAP which you can open up at anytime and track "collectables" or in general, scout ahead and make a plan of what to do and where to go... to top that off the game was made in 2013... compared to the abysmal map system of LMA in 2016. It also does not stutter when you fly, run or fall like LMA. 
⚫You also cannot do EVERY single side mission with one character, a flying character for instance. The game makes you use LAND BASED VEHICLES for LAND BASED RACES. Again, unlike LMA making vehicles USELESS.
⚫Game costs £14.99. DLC added is just about £20. The game does not FORCE you to buy ANY DLC to achieve 100% and it is not stupidly overpriced either. It is completely optional. Again... unlike LMA... that FORCES you to buy DLC to achieve 100%, LEGO® Marvel™ Super Heroes does not. 
⚫Fun for the entire family!

[h1][b] Cons [/b][/h1] 
⚫The only issue I truly had with the game was the inconsistent, confusing flight system. Using my thumbsticks it made my character move away from the camera or towards it which really annoyed me. The other part of this is that the "A" button makes you ACCELERATE and its also the button to ASCEND. This led me to face-planting a building or overshooting one of my races/objective by a mile. 
⚫I also had a little bit of stutter in some missions but it did not make to much of a difference in the end. 

[h1][b] My Verdict [/b][/h1] 
LEGO® Marvel™ Super Heroes is an absolute blast even in 2023. I found myself playing this night after night enjoying the story, collecting my gold bricks and watching Iron Man have a dance party in the Avenger's tower. This is the peak of happiness that Traveler's Tales has to offer!!

EDIT: Game did not take me 70 hours to 100%. Due to an issue with my old PC the game would not shut down, so It gained 40 hours of AFK time. So my actual 100% time is 29 hours.

[h1][b] A solid 9/10. I would recommend this game to ANY and ALL. An amazing addition to any vivid lego game collector [/b][/h1]

Lego Marvel Super Heroes is an action adventure game developed by TT games and published by Warner Brothers, releasing in 2013 on PS3, Xbox 360, Wii U, PS4 and Xbox One, and of course, PC and Mac. 

Game play is similar to that of other Lego titles, you are able to take control of around 150 characters straight out of the Marvel Universe, and each of them have their own abilities. Each of the game’s levels consist of a series of puzzles which use specific characters special abilities, as well as breaking objects to them build other items to help you traverse the environment. In between each level, you enter a free roam type area around the streets of New York. The free roam contains opportunities to complete small side missions which are narrated by none other than Deadpool.  When in the main missions, there are a few side actives to complete too as well, which include Marvel co-creator, Stan Lee; this segment of the game is called “Stan Lee in Peril”. 

The graphics in Marvel Super Heroes is very much the same as other Lego games, you will find it very hard to fault the visual department of this game; it looks colourful, animated to perfection, everything in the game is made out of Lego, so it has that childish charm that is just gorgeous. There is a wide range of resolution options, but a lack of any other graphical choices, other than texture quality which still only has two levels, high and low. 

There is really no difficulty in the game, there is no penalty for dying, since you just respawn straight away, you will be stumped for ideas on a few of the puzzles and you will just have to experiment with your characters in order to progress. The boss fights are all uniquely challenging and offer various different waves of battle for you to learn.  

The game’s level design is perfect; there is an in game “brick counter” which you can fill up by breaking other Lego objects in game for other smaller bricks. I played the game with my partner and we made it our aim to fill this counter on each level, this adds another challenge to the game, and lets you have the satisfaction of breaking tons of Lego and collecting thousands of smaller bricks. On top of this, there are also plenty of small Easter eggs too, which the odd appearance from Deadpool (who doesn’t appear as a main character in the story).

We finished the game in just under nine hours on co-op mode with collecting 100% of the bricks on each stage. What makes the Lego games repayable is that after you complete a level, you have the free play option unlocked – this means you can play as any character on that stage to unlock special areas for more side missions and collectables. Whilst on the subject of collectables, there are so many to find! On top of the regular cast of characters, there are over 100 more to find and discover whilst completing side quests, achievements, and finding items.  Complentionists will have a field day with this game.  

Sadly we did run into a few technical problems during our play through. The main one being one of the levels just freezes all of the time; this is a known bug and the only way you can progress is purely by restarting the level and hoping you are lucky – thankfully this bug is right at the start of the stage, so you don’t lose much progress.  Another issue we ran into was fairly annoying, in that characters can sometimes get stuck in the environment, this isn’t too bad if you are able to kill the character with another player, but sometimes this isn’t possible so the only way you can get around the issue is by restarting the level; this can sometimes be painstakingly annoying if you are right at the end of a stage.  We did have a positive experience both using a 360 controller and the Steam controller to play though. I would strongly recommend anyone picking this game up to use either of the two controller options. 

I have come to the conclusion that Lego really make fantastic games; and Marvel Super Heroes is no different. You have two of the biggest franchises in the world today and combined them; you have a recipe for success straight away. We had such a blast whilst playing and I would strongly recommend Lego Marvel Super Heroes to any fans of Marvel or Lego out there. The regular price of £14, 99 is spot on as well. If you can get it any cheaper, do not hesitate to pick it up, you won’t be disappointed.

It’s been a while, eh?

The story follows Loki as he seeks revenge for what happened to him in Asgard, teaming up with Galactus, Doctor Doom, and Magneto.

Story:
The story and overall concept are genuinely amazing. I had a lot of fun seeing how everything unfolded and how the narrative developed from the beginning to the end. That said, it wasn’t anything truly special on its own. What made it stand out was the inclusion of the X-Men, Galactus, the Fantastic Four, and the Avengers. If the game had focused on only one of these groups, it would have felt bland and incomplete.

Gameplay:
The gameplay was fun for the first 6–7 missions, but after that it became repetitive especially the boss fights. Toward the end, the main reason I kept playing was simply to finish the game and for the nostalgia.

Level Design:
There is some clever level design present, but much like the combat and gameplay, it starts to feel very similar over time. The settings change, but the puzzles and patterns largely stay the same.

World Design:
The world design is impressive. The city felt alive and enjoyable to explore, and the mission settings were extremely creative and fun to experience.

Visuals:
Surprisingly good for a 12-year-old game.

Performance:
I played on the highest settings at 1440p and 120 FPS on a mid-range PC. There were some FPS drops in certain missions, but overall performance was solid and acceptable.

Difficulty Balance:
No major issues here. The difficulty felt well balanced, and there isn’t much to criticize. That said, I genuinely don’t know how I managed to solve some of the puzzles back then they’re easy now, but I remember struggling a lot at the time.

Value:
I bought the game during a sale for a very low price and don’t regret it at all. However, I would never pay full price for a game that is now 12–13 years old.

Typical LEGO game where you have different characters with different special skills that need to be used throughout the game so you can solve the simple puzzles placed throughout the 15 levels of the story mode.  The big difference here is the number of characters that you can unlock, the additional Deadpool levels that you can play, and the open world New York City with tons of side quests that you can take on.  The game is huge.  The story is fun and new and it gives you a great reason to play as your favorite super heroes.

This is one of those games that screams to be played with another player and my kids loved every minute of it.

Whether you're a LEGO fan, a Marvel fan, both, or neither; this game is an enjoyable piece of fun worth your time.

Admittedly, it will appeal more to you if you're familiar with the Marvel universes. The characters, the stories, the references; they all shout Marvel. But it's the combination with the LEGO franchise and mechanisms that brings the real fun and jokes!

In this game, you will play through 15 levels, each chapter with its designated duo of characters. But once you've finished the level, you can play it again with any character you want, which is needed to find some of the more hidden collectibles. And there is a mass of characters to choose from, each with their own abilities (although most abilities are available to multiple characters.) You will have to collect these characters though before they become playable, and this is where the mainpart of the overworld comes in besides the connection between chapters: This LEGO Marvel version of Manhattan is crowded with side quests, races, hidden objectives, and so much more. Just exploring the overworld alone is a lot of fun.

Most achievements you'll get from just playing the game, but there are a few that will make you collect everything possible to collect and search in every nook of Manhattan and the levels. I managed to 100% the game in just a little under 50 hours, and it never was boresome or tiring.

And if you need any help, Deadpool's there for you. If you can find him.

In order to answer these questions, I have and will tackle all the older games again and write something about them.

To answer the question of whether the games are worth it in advance:
[b]I think yes, definitely[/b], even if the game is from 2011 and has been around for a few days and is of course no longer graphically convincing. [b]If the games are cheap and you like playing Lego games then they should not be missing in your collection.[/b]

With countless characters and their different (combat) characteristics that you unlock in the course of the game, the story campaign has [b]15 levels against Dr. Doom and his gang.[/b]
As the title of the game already suggests, all Marvel heroes fight side by side and not only have to save New York from impending disaster, but the whole world.
The diverse levels are usually divided into three sections, have a save option at the beginning of each section and offer a lot of visual and playful variety.
Away from the story, there is a lot to discover, collect and unlock in and around New York.

For the pure story in the first run you need about 10-12 hours of play. For collecting all minikits and rescuing Stan Lee in each mission, as well as exploring the open world with all missions and unlockables, you can pack a lot of time on it.

In Lego Marvel Super Heroes there are several ways to reach your goal of 100% completion of the game.
After the story you have the opportunity to hang around in New York and collect enough golden bricks to unlock the Deadpool missions. 
These Missions brings you the coveted red bricks with the multiplicators or the stone and miniktite detectors.
But since [b]the game is so easy, I find that you can play through the levels well in free play without the detectors and find everything without help.[/b]
But of course you can do whatever you want.

[b]This is my second time playing the game and I can't quite remember if I enjoyed it more the first time.[/b]
Yes, it's Lego of the old school and it's fun the Lego way as always, but it just doesn't win me over like some other Lego games.

I find the puzzles extremely easy and also boring, [b]the game helps you in every imaginable way so that you never really have to think about how to proceed.[/b]
The AI is constantly in your way so that you don't see exactly what you're doing or it's stuck somewhere and can't keep up. 
Switching back and forth between the characters is sometimes a bit stressful until you have chosen the right one.

But towards the end I found the “Magneto Gang” the most annoying. Especially the one with the red hair ([u]nothing against red hair, it's just the looks of said character[/u]).
You are constantly under siege and have to fight your way out again and again before you can do something, unless someone is hiding somewhere and freezes or disassembles you...
Sometimes I just found it exhausting, annoying and boring.

But what I can still remember from the first round is the stupid flying with Iron Man.
Yes, I'm not that much of a flier, I admit, and I dread it in every game when I have to fly around with such a small character. In other, newer Lego games, this is now much better. It's a disaster for me here. 
Using the buttons to steer up and down instead of the stick drives me crazy and I often overshoot the target or don't get the curve right.

[b]I don't mean to badmouth the game, absolutely not. I just think there are definitely better Lego games out there that are a lot more fun. [/b]
Of course, one must not forget that the game dates back to 2013 and is therefore one of the older games and cannot be technically compared to newer games. But that is subjective.

All in all, [b]a mixed game for me[/b]. Not bad and, apart from the things mentioned that I don't like that much, it's fun as always.

If you’ve played any LEGO game before, you probably know what to expect and honestly, that’s not a bad thing. This game is very enjoyable, and the unlockables keep you interested, but there are several bugs that force you to restart the game entirely, and this game's "comedy" is extremely childish and annoying. [h1] Gameplay [/h1]
It's the classic LEGO gameplay - not as developed as later titles but it's still good and for some aspects (eg. combat) I prefer it. Most of the puzzles are intuitive however a few are unclear which feels like they were still getting to grips with the open world format. The driving is a highlight for me with the races being some of my favourite missions.

[h1] Story [/h1]
Decent story, cutscenes get a bit annoying after you've seen them a few times but you can skip them in free play so it doesn't really matter. Bonus points for including the X-Men & Fantastic Four which is nice to see for someone who is less familiar with them. 

[h1] World [/h1]
I love the world of this game and it's actually what inspired me to get it on Steam. It's set in Manhattan NY and while I don't know how it pairs to the real thing it feels like it could be a real city if it wasn't for all the LEGO. Speaking of which, there are small little LEGO details all over the map which are fun to discover as you look for all of the collectibles. It's quite fun to just drive around smashing things for studs too.

[h1] Characters [/h1]
There are over 100 characters available to collect in this game ranging from the classic familiar ones you'd expect (Iron Man, Captain America etc.) to some more obscure characters that I had never heard of. There's even a wide array of vehicles (cars, bikes, boats, planes and helicopters) available too.

[h1] Graphics [/h1]
The graphics of this game have held up quite well considering it's turning 10 years old soon - obviously nothing's mind-blowing but it all looks fine and I actually really like how the effects look for the superpower abilities. Some of the far away buildings render strangely in Manhattan but I don't think that's a problem and they all look fine close up.

[h1] Achievements [/h1]
Really good achievements: most of them directly correlate with progression (good choice if you want to go for 100% achievements) and then there are a few that involve doing specific challenges which I found to be quite fun. No grindy achievements unless you consider 100% completion grindy - but it doesn't feel like it's too much effort. 

[h1] Conclusion / TLDR [/h1]
A very solid LEGO game: while you can tell they were still getting to grips with the open world formula it is thoroughly enjoyable and a very fun game to go for 100% completion in. Strongly recommend.

[h1]THE ONE SENTENCE SUMMARY[/h1]
[i]LEGO MARVEL Super Heroes[/i] is a super enjoyable game because of the things it does well—only slightly hindered by the things that haven’t aged well since its release in 2013.

[h1][➕] THE POSITIVES[/h1]
+ [b]IT’S A LEGO GAME.[/b] LEGO games have a long-established formula that has worked well for over two decades. The games are all about collecting, building, and feeling rewarded for EVERYTHING you do. If you enjoy LEGO and the subject matter, you’ll enjoy the game!

+ [b]The LEVEL DESIGN.[/b] The game has 14 story missions which are super well-designed! The puzzles force you to approach each with the different tools (i.e. characters) at your disposal—both in the story and freeplay exploration. They’re built in intuitive ways without overcomplicating the experience, and are, overall, super fun!

+ [b]The STORY.[/b] While it flirts with the premise established by the [i]Avengers[/i] movie (as one might expect), it does a good job of building its own story in otherwise familiar settings. It also very much feels like a “comic book” story, which is (obviously) important as a comic book superhero game.

+ [b]The CHARACTERS.[/b] Many of my favorite super heroes (and villains) make an appearance with all the rich personality and goofiness expected from a LEGO game. Loki, Spider-Man, Thor, and others make appearances—including [i]the best[/i] kitty who (briefly) steals the show!
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2270674569
+ [b]FLYING AROUND NEW YORK is AWESOME![/b] The ability to zoom around as Iron Man or Swing as Spidey between the skyscrapers is AWESOME—a really cool way to explore the world when you’re between missions.
	
+ [b]The ability to “ENABLE” OPEN-WORLD EXPLORATION.[/b] In earlier LEGO games, you’d be locked into “story mode” (and the specific characters available in the current chapter) until you finished the game, when you’d unlock the ability to swap characters freely in the open world. In [i]MARVEL Super Heroes[/i], you only need to visit a changing station to explore freely—a most welcome change for players who want to swap between exploring and advancing the story!

+ [b]AGENT COULSON.[/b] They got [i]THE[/I] Clark Gregg to voice Agent Coulson, which is simply wonderful… He sounds great, so he’s a great addition to the game!

+ [b]MUSIC and AUDIO DESIGN.[/b] The music is [i]wonderfully[/i] “Avengers-esque!” It fits the heroic moments and captures that New York feel in the open world. And the audio design—as with any LEGO game—does a great job of rounding out the world.

+ [b]The HELICARRIER.[/b] It’s fun to see the helicarrier not only make an appearance in the game, but serve as the base of operations for your adventures!

+ [b]DEADPOOL.[/b] What a delightful dork…!

[h1][〰] THE..."TAKE IT OR LEAVE IT"[/h1]
~ [b]IRON MAN’S VO.[/b] While most of the voices are [reasonably] voice-matched to what we’re used to in the movies, Iron Man’s voice is the exception. While there’s no precedent that says it [i]has[/i] to sound like Robert Downey Jr., it feels anomalous when the rest of the voice cast “fits” their characters so well.

~ [b]I’d like to be able to ZOOM OUT THE MAP further.[/b] The in-game map is a super useful tool when it comes to tracking tasks, bricks, and characters to collect. Unfortunately, it feels super claustrophobic: only allowing you to zoom out far enough to see an extra city block or two—not nearly enough to get a true, bird’s eye view of New York City!

~ [b]GAME STABILITY.[/b] While the game does a better job than earlier titles of not crashing or disrupting your play, you can still expect stability issues. Fortunately, the game quick-saves often enough to counteract most unexpected disruptions, which does help alleviate the sting.

~ [b]Character “SKILLS” ARE NOT CLEAR.[/b] One of the aspects of LEGO games that has become popular is the character “skill” system—where characters have certain abilities that come in handy throughout the game. While this adds an intriguing element to the experience, [i]Marvel Super Heroes[/i] doesn’t make it clear [b]which[/b] characters have [b]what[/b] powers. This means you’ll be using the handful of characters that can accomplish most of your needs (i.e. Iron Man) while struggling to find those with the one, unique power to complete certain, specific challenges (i.e. mind control).

~ [b]A way to QUICKLY “RESTART” RACES would be [i]super[/i] welcome.[/b] Due to the clunky driving and flight controls (see below), you’ll probably be restarting races quite often. Sometimes you’ll fail super late in a race, leaving you stranded miles away from the starting point. A mechanic that allows you to quickly reset and restart the races would be most welcome!

[h1][➖] THE NOT-SO-GREAT[/h1]
[b]⚠ WARNING: The game defaults to a 1280X720 resolution. ⚠[/b] Consider closing out all your other windows until you’ve launched the game and fixed the resolution. Otherwise, enjoy everything being squished into Monitor 1…! 🤦‍♂️

- [b]TARGETING certain GOLD OBJECTS or WATER POOLS requires EXTREME precision.[/b] The targeting zone can be EXTREMELY small, requiring you to target very specific pixels on your screen. It’s not as generous as other LEGO games, making it a frustrating mechanic.

- [b]FLYING AND DRIVING CONTROLS are VERY clunky.[/b] Flying feels like you’re steering an out-of-control missile, while driving feels like you’re steering a vehicle that can only turn in the cardinal directions and gets stuck on any obstacle.

As a note: races will often be easier in single-player, as you’ll be able to see the upcoming gates well in advance (which is significantly more challenging when you’re working with half the screen).

- [b]RED BRICKS DON’T STAY ENABLED on re-launch.[/b] A minor annoyance, but having to re-enable the Red Bricks every time you launch the game is a minor frustration—PARTICULARLY since you’ll be resetting the game due to crashes and other errors later on.

- [b]Inability to SCROLL BETWEEN CHARACTER VARIANTS.[/b] To avoid a massive character screen, [i]LEGO Marvel Super Heroes[/i] “stacks” similar characters on top of each other.

For example, there are [i]eight[/i] variants of the Iron Man “suits.”

As you unlock more powerful variants, you’ll eventually pick one or two of the best versions…which means waiting for them to auto-scroll around to your favorite rather than being able to manually scroll through the gallery of characters. Though minor, it is a consistent annoyance.

- [b]NO ABILITY TO DISABLE HINTS.[/b] This means you’ll be getting Coulson’s “helpful” reminders constantly; and while they’ll occasionally point you in the right direction to complete a challenge, it can get annoying to be re-re-re-taught how to melt gold bricks for the full 30+ hours of gameplay.

- [b]QUESTS and RACES often disrupt Player 2.[/b] While less common than earlier LEGO games, there is still the random quest giver or race that breaks a timer or takes over the full screen. It’s [i]usually[/i] to highlight something important, but still feels disruptive in two-player mode.

- [b]Random, one off GAME BUGS.[/b] Characters getting locked out of elevators... Mind-controlled characters disappearing... Certain quests only displaying in single player mode—forcing the second player to drop out briefly. As one of the older games in the series, be ready to run into (and work around) a handful of bugs that will impede or halt your progress from time to time.

[h1][🙂] THE FINAL WORD…[/h1]
If you enjoy stud collecting, the feeling of being rewarded for anything (and everything) you do, other LEGO games, or Marvel comics, you’ll enjoy this game regardless of its problems. And ultimately, it captures the most important thing that makes LEGO games so sticky: [b]IT'S FUN[/b]—especially as a two-player game or one to play with your family!
